findings.title: verify does not enforce session expiry
findings.description: verify returns a session as long as its token matches, even after expires_at has passed. Expired tokens therefore remain accepted indefinitely.

findings.title: require_admin always returns False
findings.description: The condition uses `or`, so every role fails at least one comparison and the method never admits a session, including admins and owners.

findings.title: revoke crashes on unknown tokens
findings.description: del self.sessions[token] raises KeyError when the token is not present. An idempotent revoke call on an already-removed or unknown token crashes instead of no-opping.

findings.title: bearer_token crashes on missing or malformed headers
findings.description: Indexing split result at position 1 raises IndexError for an empty or single-token Authorization header. main.handle calls this on every request, so unauthenticated requests crash rather than receiving 401.

findings.title: eviction does not pick the LRU entry
findings.description: victim is always the first inserted key rather than the entry with the oldest `used` timestamp, contradicting the documented least-recently-used eviction.

findings.title: sweep mutates the cache while iterating it
findings.description: Deleting entries during a direct iteration of self.entries raises RuntimeError whenever an expired entry exists. This crashes the janitor sweep.

findings.title: utilization is almost always 0 and divides by zero for an empty limit
findings.description: Integer division discards any partial utilization, so a non-full cache reports 0 percent. A configured limit of 0 also raises ZeroDivisionError.

findings.title: flush deadlocks by re-entering a non-reentrant lock
findings.description: flush holds self.lock and then calls self.delete, which tries to acquire the same threading.Lock again. The admin flush endpoint hangs forever.

findings.title: LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS is stored as milliseconds, not seconds
findings.description: The environment value is documented as milliseconds, but it is assigned directly to cfg.timeout, whose default is 10 seconds. A 10000 ms request becomes a 10000-second timeout.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is not converted from milliseconds
findings.description: The parsed millisecond duration is stored as cfg.cache_ttl while the default is 300 seconds, producing TTLs 1000x too long when configured.

findings.title: cache TTL and size parsing are unguarded and can crash startup
findings.description: int(ttl) and int(size) are called without handling ValueError, unlike the port and timeout fields. A malformed environment value aborts startup instead of falling back to defaults.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but never applied
findings.description: parsed is validated but never assigned to cfg.fetch_limit, so fetch_limit can never change from 32.

findings.title: load_file leaks the config file handle and can crash on bad values
findings.description: open(path).read() is never explicitly closed, and int(value.strip()) can raise on malformed input. A malformed line should be ignored, not crash loading.

findings.title: validate always reports success
findings.description: validate prints configuration problems but unconditionally returns True, so callers cannot tell that startup configuration is invalid.

findings.title: write_snapshot leaves the handle open and renames before flushing
findings.description: The temporary file handle is never closed or flushed before os.rename, and no fsync is performed. Buffered data may never reach disk, defeating the atomic durability guarantee.

findings.title: read_report leaks the opened file handle
findings.description: open(...).read() returns the contents but does not ensure the file is closed in all implementations, leaking descriptors on repeated reads.

findings.title: parse_report has a mutable default and emits a blank trailing row
findings.description: The default rows=[] is shared across calls, so rows accumulate between invocations. The trailing empty line produced by split is also converted into an empty dict row.

findings.title: stats endpoint divides by zero on an empty store
findings.description: store.size() and cache.utilization() can be zero, making hits_per_link and cache percentage raise ZeroDivisionError on an empty or unconfigured service.

findings.title: report reads under the original name after defaulting the write name
findings.description: export_csv changes an empty name to "links", but read_report uses the original empty name, looking for ".csv" and failing to read the report that was just written.

findings.title: create uses a mutable default tag list
findings.description: tags=[] is evaluated once, so links created without explicit tags share the same list. Mutating one link's tags mutates the default used for future links.

findings.title: create crashes for a first-time owner
findings.description: self.quota[owner] + 1 raises KeyError when owner has no previous quota entry, so the first link for any new owner fails.

findings.title: resolve deletes live links and keeps expired ones
findings.description: The expiry test is inverted: it deletes the link when it is still valid and returns None, while expired links survive and increment hits. This deletes good links on normal redirects and revives expired codes.

findings.title: rename validates the source code twice instead of the destination
findings.description: validate_code(frm) is called twice and to is never validated, so invalid destination codes can be introduced by renaming.

findings.title: success_rate truncates every non-100 percent result to zero
findings.description: Integer floor division before multiplication makes any rate below 100 percent report as 0 percent.

findings.title: delete does not refund the owner quota
findings.description: Deleting a link removes it from self.links but never decrements self.quota, so owners cannot create new links after deleting old ones despite the documented behavior.

findings.title: top returns least-used links first
findings.description: Sorting ascending and taking the first n returns the lowest-hit links, the opposite of the leaderboard's intended ordering.

findings.title: by_owner matches owners by substring
findings.description: The predicate `owner in l.owner` matches any owner whose name contains the requested substring, leaking links across similarly named owners.

findings.title: extend revives already expired links
findings.description: extend always pushes expires_at into the future, violating the documented rule that an expired link stays expired.

findings.title: quotas exposes the internal mutable dict
findings.description: Returning self.quota directly lets callers mutate store state, contradicting the snapshot contract.

findings.title: import_all is not atomic and skips quota updates
findings.description: Links are inserted one at a time without validation-first or rollback, and owner quotas are never updated. A later invalid code leaves earlier imports in place.

findings.title: prune mutates the dictionary while iterating and returns the wrong count
findings.description: Deleting self.links entries during iteration raises RuntimeError when expired links exist, and the method returns the number of surviving links instead of the number removed.

findings.title: find_expired returns a generator over a mutating mapping
findings.description: The janitor iterates this generator while deleting entries from self.links, which raises RuntimeError. The generator is also unsafe for callers that store the result.

findings.title: warm_cache returns before probe threads finish
findings.description: Threads are started but never joined, so callers proceed while cache writes are still in flight, violating the documented contract.

findings.title: check_targets crashes when no targets fail
findings.description: Returning problems[0] raises IndexError when every link target is https, so the empty/non-failing case is unusable.

findings.title: count_for_owner crashes for owners with no links
findings.description: Indexing quotas()[owner] raises KeyError instead of reporting 0 for owners absent from the quota map.

findings.title: Authenticator.sessions is unprotected shared mutable state
findings.description: issue(), verify(), revoke(), and require_admin() access self.sessions concurrently without synchronization. Request threads can mutate the dict while verify() iterates it, causing RuntimeError or lost updates; revoke() can also delete a token concurrent with issue() or verify().

findings.title: Cache.flush deadlocks by reacquiring its own non-reentrant lock
findings.description: flush() holds self.lock and then calls self.delete(), which attempts to acquire the same threading.Lock again. Any thread reaching the admin flush endpoint will deadlock permanently.

findings.title: Cache.sweep mutates the dict while iterating it
findings.description: While holding the lock, sweep() iterates self.entries and deletes entries from it during traversal. Python raises RuntimeError once an expired entry is encountered; the same pattern also appears in Store.prune().

findings.title: Cache peek(), stats(), and utilization() bypass the lock
findings.description: These methods read self.entries and self.hits while other methods mutate them under the lock. They violate the class's thread-safety contract and can observe stale or inconsistent cache state.

findings.title: Cache.warm has an unlocked check-then-act race
findings.description: warm() calls unlocked peek() and then locked set(). Concurrent warm() calls can both observe absence and both insert, oversubscribing the cache and racing on eviction.

findings.title: Store.links and Store.quota are unprotected shared mutable state
findings.description: All Store methods mutate and read self.links and self.quota without synchronization. HTTP request threads and the janitor thread can race on dict iteration, insertion, deletion, and quota updates, corrupting storage.

findings.title: Store.find_expired returns a live view consumed while mutating
findings.description: find_expired() returns a generator over self.links.items(). The janitor iterates it and deletes from self.links, which mutates the underlying dict during iteration and can raise RuntimeError or skip entries.

findings.title: Metrics counters are incremented and read without synchronization
findings.description: add_resolved(), add_created(), and snapshot() operate on unsynchronized integer fields. Concurrent resolve/create paths can lose increments, and snapshot() can read partial values.

findings.title: Janitor thread directly mutates store links and has unsafe global lifecycle
findings.description: The janitor loop deletes entries from store.links outside store locking and relies on global _running/_janitor. Repeated start_janitor() calls leak previous threads and lose their references, while expired-cleanup races with request traffic.

findings.title: warm_cache returns before its worker threads finish
findings.description: Threads are started but never joined, so warm_cache() returns while threads may still be mutating the cache. This violates its documented completion behavior and can leave writes running after the caller continues.

findings.title: write_snapshot uses a shared temporary file path
findings.description: All callers use the fixed path /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json. Concurrent snapshot writes interleave in the same file and rename races can expose partial or stale snapshot data.

findings.title: Hard-coded fallback session secret
findings.description: When LINKD_SECRET is unset, the authenticator falls back to the publicly known string 'dev-secret-do-not-use'. Any deployment that forgets to set the env var can be attacked with a credential committed to source.

findings.title: Session token generated with non-cryptographic RNG
findings.description: issue() builds tokens from random.getrandbits(), whose Mersenne Twister state can be recovered from observed outputs. Because tokens gate every endpoint, an attacker who collects enough tokens can predict future sessions.

findings.title: Session token written to logs
findings.description: issued tokens are printed with print(). Anyone with log/stdout access can replay a live token and hijack the session.

findings.title: Token expiry is never enforced
findings.description: verify() compares only the token value and ignores expires_at, so sessions live forever and stolen tokens cannot be aged out.

findings.title: Password hashed with unsalted SHA-256
findings.description: hash_password() uses a single fast SHA-256 digest with no salt, making stored hashes trivially brute-forced and enabling rainbow-table lookup after any database leak.

findings.title: bearer_token crashes on malformed or missing header
findings.description: The function blindly indexes the second split field. In handle() this is called before any guard, so a request with no or malformed Authorization header raises an unhandled exception and may leak a stack trace.

findings.title: secret_equals not actually constant time
findings.description: The helper is documented as leak-free but uses ==, allowing a timing attack that recovers the expected secret byte by byte when it is invoked.

findings.title: validate() always reports success even for bad config
findings.description: problems are printed but the function returns True unconditionally, so invalid or insecure configuration still starts the service instead of failing at deploy time.

findings.title: Permissive CORS combined with credentials
findings.description: The response sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Browsers may not enforce it consistently, and the configuration signals that any origin is trusted with credentialed requests.

findings.title: Unknown token reflected in 401 response
findings.description: The 401 body includes the submitted token verbatim. This exposes the presented credential in responses and logs and can aid token enumeration or phishing.

findings.title: Link owner taken from request body instead of session
findings.description: create_link() uses payload['owner'] rather than the authenticated session's owner. Any authenticated user can attribute a link to another user, consume that user's quota, or impersonate them.

findings.title: Deletion has no ownership check
findings.description: delete_link() deletes any code without comparing it to the session owner, so an authenticated user can delete other users' links by guessing or knowing their codes.

findings.title: Open redirect via next parameter
findings.description: The /out endpoint places the user-supplied next value directly into the Location header, enabling phishing where an attacker sends victims a trusted link that redirects to an attacker site.

findings.title: Admin endpoint authorized by spoofable header
findings.description: admin_quotas() grants access when x-admin is 'true', a header any client can set, bypassing authentication entirely for the admin quota data.

findings.title: Error response leaks internal path and exception
findings.description: The export failure response includes cfg.export_dir and the underlying IOError text, disclosing filesystem layout and internals to callers.

findings.title: Path traversal in report name
findings.description: export_csv() concatenates user-supplied name into a filesystem path without sanitization, so a name like '../../etc/passwd' can write CSV data outside export_dir. read_report() has the same issue for reads.

findings.title: Path traversal via owner in archive_all
findings.description: The owner value is used directly as a filename, so a malicious owner such as '../admin' can create or overwrite files outside the intended directory.

findings.title: Sensitive reports world-readable
findings.description: Files are created with default permissions despite containing every owner's links, contradicting the comment that only the service user may read them.

findings.title: Predictable /tmp path and TOCTOU in snapshot write
findings.description: write_snapshot() writes to a fixed, world-writable /tmp path before renaming. An attacker can pre-create a symlink there to redirect the write and truncate/replace an arbitrary file.

findings.title: CSV formula injection in exported reports
findings.description: Target/owner/code values are written unescaped. A target beginning with =,+,-, or @ is interpreted as a formula when the CSV is opened in a spreadsheet.

findings.title: by_owner uses substring match causing data leak
findings.description: Filtering uses `owner in l.owner`, so querying owner 'a' returns links owned by 'admin', 'alice', etc. Support handoff of one owner's data therefore leaks other owners' links.

findings.title: quotas() exposes mutable internal state
findings.description: Returning the live quota dict lets callers mutate counts directly, breaking ownership/ quotas and integrity assumptions.

findings.title: extend() revives expired links
findings.description: extend() sets expires_at = now + ttl unconditionally, bringing a dead code back to life even though expiry is documented as final.

findings.title: Short codes minted from predictable RNG
findings.description: new_code() uses random.getrandbits(), so codes are predictable enough to enumerate, allowing attackers to discover and resolve short links without knowing them.
